answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by fingerprinting each machine's hardware clock skew. Every quartz crystal drifts at a slightly different rate, so the tiny offset in TCP timestamps forms a velvet signature no two hosts share. Honest agents in a meadow each run on distinct hardware, while a Sybil farm's identities all tick with one shared skew. The network measures drift each epoch and merges same-skew identities into one reward slot. Forging a new skew means buying another machine, so cost grows linearly, like building a separate mesa per fake town. One clock, one reward.
